entries.source: SDK 26.2, MPNowPlayingInfoLanguageOption.h, MP_API(ios(9.0), tvos(9.0), macos(10.12.2), watchos(5.0))
entries.reason: THE RELEASE CARRIES NO SUCH CLASS, at both ends, read CLASS-SCOPED rather than from a name list: tools/corpus/objc-inventory.lua over the armv7 dyld shared caches of 6.1.3 and 4.3 reads MPNowPlayingInfoLanguageOption ABSENT from both. Each read carried its controls in the same run - MPVolumeView and MPMediaPlaylist read PRESENT on both ends, and MPNowPlayingInfoCenter reads PRESENT at 6.1.3 and ABSENT at 4.3, so the reader discriminates rather than answering yes to everything it is shown. The whole-cache selector list (selectors_armv7.txt, 113981 DISTINCT NAMES) could not have decided this: a name is on one line if ANY class anywhere declares it, so a one there says nothing about the owner and only a zero means absence from the release. A class no release has is new code and cannot shadow anything, so there is nothing native for it to be, and `absent` - which is for a row whose answer needs a thing the device lacks - is the wrong word: nothing here needs one. WHAT MAKES IT MORE THAN A DECLARATION is that the release carries the inputs it is built from, read at CLASS level in the same two runs: AVMediaSelectionOption is PRESENT at 6.1.3 with 24 own instance methods including -locale, -mediaType, -hasMediaCharacteristic:, -displaysNonForcedSubtitles and -isPlayable, and AVMediaSelectionGroup is PRESENT with 18 own methods including -options, allowsEmptySelection and -_defaultOption. So the class is a value holder over state the release really has, and not an invented answer to a question the device cannot answer. THE TWO 'automatic' ACCESSORS ANSWER NO, MEASURED AGAINST APPLE'S OWN CLASS: MPNowPlayingInfoLanguageOption.h:56-63 documents each as 'a special case that is used to represent the best legible/audible language option based on system preferences', so what each asks is whether the receiver IS that option, and the option the system inserts to mean 'choose for me' is not one a caller can build - neither in Apple's framework nor here. tests/backports/host/mp-language-option builds all 34 options Apple's own designated initialiser can build (13 tags x both types, the nil tag, nil/empty/filled characteristics, displayName and identifier, and an option installed as a group's default) and Apple's MediaPlayer answers NO to every one, with the type round-tripping as the control that makes those NOs answers rather than a dropped argument. The tag constant the header names, MPLangaugeOptionAutoLangaugeTag, is DECLARED NOWHERE in the SDK and its value is not written down here; what the system inserts is not askable from outside on either side
entries.effect: NSClassFromString answers the class, [MPNowPlayingInfoLanguageOption new] allocates a real object instead of messaging nil, and the five declared accessors read what the caller stored. MPChangeLanguageOptionCommandEvent90.m, already on main, declares an MPNowPlayingInfoLanguageOption * property whose type this file makes real - before it, that property could only ever hold nil

entries.source: SDK 26.2, MPNowPlayingInfoLanguageOption.h, MP_API(ios(9.0), tvos(9.0), macos(10.12.2), watchos(5.0))
entries.reason: read CLASS-SCOPED with tools/corpus/objc-inventory.lua over the armv7 caches of 6.1.3 and 4.3, this class reads ABSENT from both, with the controls named in the MPNowPlayingInfoLanguageOption row in the same two runs - so the zero is the release's and not the reader's. A class no release has is new code and cannot shadow anything, which is what lets it be `implemented` over `absent`. It is built over the same real state as its element class: AVMediaSelectionGroup is PRESENT at 6.1.3 and its own 18 methods include -options and -allowsEmptySelection, the two things this group holds. The header calls it 'a mutually exclusive group of language options' where 'only one language option within a given group may be active at a time' (:86-87), and this object does NOT enforce that: it holds the set the caller built and the one option the caller marked active, because enforcing exclusivity would mean silently dropping options the caller passed, which is a different API from the one Apple declares
entries.effect: NSClassFromString answers the class and a caller-built group holds the options, the default and the allowEmptySelection flag it was given, copied so a later mutation of the caller's array cannot change what the group reads
